# check/ensure

> Postcondition: ensure cond stops the program, saying where and what, if cond is false.

truck [check](../check.md) · [source](../../../registry/check/ensure.pkg)

Use it before returning, for what a function promises:

```
fn sorted_copy(xs: [int]) -> [int]
  let out = ...
  ensure is_sorted(out)
  return out
end
```

If the condition is false, the program writes the position, the
condition as written, and the message after it, to stderr, and exits
with status 2:

```
app.pkg:12:3: ensure failed: n >= 0 && n <= len(xs): n is out of range
```

The message is any number of `str` expressions, written one after
another, and evaluated only when the check fails: `require n > 0, "got ",
show(n)` with `strfmt`. Swap `use check` for
`use nocheck` to turn every check into nothing (the conditions are
still type-checked).

## Syntax

Kind: `statement`

```
ensure {c: expr bool} [ , {m: expr str} ]*
```

| slot | takes | type |
|---|---|---|
| `c` | expression | `bool` |
| `m` (optional) | expression | `str` |

## Expands to

This package has no backend: each use is rewritten to the following
source, with `{slot}` replaced by what was written there, and compiled again.

```
if !{c}
check_fail({@pos}, "ensure failed", {quote c})
{each g in ,}
check_note({g.m})
{end}
check_stop()
end
```
